subject: Mathematics
summary: Comprehensive coverage from Kuratowski ordered pairs (a, b) ≡ {{a}, {a, b}} and Cartesian products A × B to total binary relations 2ᵐⁿ, structural function axioms (totality & single-valuedness), vertical line test, standard real functions (Modulus, Signum, GIF, Fractional Part, Logarithms), systematic domain & range toolkits, composite algebra (g ∘ f)(x), 7 NEST exam traps, master glossary, and 20 practice questions.
chapterCommonMistakes: Trap 1: Confusing Non-Commutativity of Cartesian Products. A × B ≠ B × A unless A = B or one set is empty.
Trap 2: Forgetting the Empty Relation (∅) and Identity Relation in counting binary relations. Total relations = 2ᵐⁿ.
Trap 3: Assuming Codomain equals Range. Range = {f(x) | x ∈ A} ⊆ B (Codomain).
Trap 4: Missing the Vertical Line Test for Functionality. If any vertical line intersects the curve at more than 1 point, it fails single-valuedness.
Trap 5: Incorrect GIF Floor Simplification: ⌊x + k⌋ = ⌊x⌋ + k holds ONLY for integer k ∈ ℤ.
Trap 6: Assuming Dom(g ∘ f) equals Dom(f). Rigorous domain: Dom(g ∘ f) = {x ∈ Dom(f) | f(x) ∈ Dom(g)}.
Trap 7: Forgetting Base Restrictions in Logarithmic Equations: log_b(a) requires BOTH a > 0, b > 0, AND b ≠ 1.

keyTerms.definition: A pair of elements (a, b) where order matters, axiomatically defined as {{a}, {a, b}}.
The set of all ordered pairs (a, b) with a ∈ A and b ∈ B.
Any subset R ⊆ A × B. The total number of relations is 2ᵐⁿ where |A| = m, |B| = n.
The set of all first coordinates of elements in relation R: {a ∈ A | ∃b ∈ B, (a, b) ∈ R}.
The set of all second coordinates of elements in relation R: {b ∈ B | ∃a ∈ A, (a, b) ∈ R}.
The entire target set B to which elements of A are related.
The relation from B to A obtained by reversing all pairs: {(b, a) | (a, b) ∈ R}.
A relation satisfying Totality (every a ∈ A is mapped) and Single-Valuedness (each a has a unique image b).
A geometric criterion: a curve is the graph of a function if and only if every vertical line intersects it at most once.
Returns x for x ≥ 0 and -x for x < 0. Dom = ℝ, Rng = [0, ∞).
Returns +1 for x > 0, 0 for x = 0, -1 for x < 0. Dom = ℝ, Rng = {-1, 0, 1}.
The largest integer less than or equal to x. Step-wise discontinuous at integers.
Defined as {x} = x - ⌊x⌋. Periodic with period 1, Dom = ℝ, Rng = [0, 1).
Function (g ∘ f)(x) = g(f(x)) defined for all x ∈ Dom(f) such that f(x) ∈ Dom(g).
Distinct domain elements map to distinct codomain elements: f(a) = f(b) ⟹ a = b.
Every element in codomain B is the image of at least one element in domain A: Range = Codomain.
A function that is simultaneously injective and surjective, guaranteeing an inverse function f⁻¹.
A function satisfying f(-x) = -f(x), symmetric about the origin.
A function satisfying f(-x) = f(x), symmetric about the y-axis.
